elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "Client may assign or transfer this Agreement ... without the prior approval of TrueLink, to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or equity"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer ... without the prior written approval of Client, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and in no event to a competitor of Client"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "No change of control of Client shall ... give TrueLink any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Vendor side is consent-gated with no successor carve-out: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer any of its rights or obligations ... without the prior written approval of Client"
Customer successor assignment is "without the prior approval of TrueLink" with no notice obligation stated

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Any other assignment by Client shall require the prior written approval of TrueLink, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld"

offending_extra_words: No change of control of Client shall constitute an assignment
Any other assignment by Client shall require the prior written approval of TrueLink, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld.
reasons: All five atomic preferred elements are met on the operative text, so the locked preferred level is satisfied.
Fallback is not satisfied (no mutual successor assignment right for Vendor and no written-notice mechanic), but the two levels are separate bargains and preferred is the target.
Minimality fails: the edit is a full-clause rewrite expanding 37 words to 124 (ratio 3.35) with changed-character ratio 0.775, exceeding the official gates.

Beyond-position additions inflate the edit: a deemed-assignment rule for change of control, "reorganization", "or equity", "in whole or in part", and "suspend or re-price" go past the preferred ask of no Vendor termination right; the restated "Any other assignment by Client" consent sentence duplicates the original default.

Intent is preserved: the unrelated mutual-consent baseline survives for other assignments, no undefined terms or dangling mechanics are introduced, and dropping Vendor's affiliate carve-out favours Customer.
